---
title: "Calorimetry and thermal assessment"
subtitle: "Paired absorption-heat data, fit membership and the remaining high-temperature bias"
---

::: {.callout-note}
Heat values are finite-dose total-enthalpy differences on the pinned Engine
(wheel `b66c7b96`): the Engine's record-anchored total enthalpy
([ePC-SAFT #84](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/84),
[#138](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/138)) with MEA's neutral
ideal-gas records and ions completed from the R1–R5 reaction enthalpies. They do
not by themselves validate an absorber model.
:::

# Question

Does the exploratory nine-species bundle reproduce absorption heat across
loading and temperature, and which heat observations were actually allowed to
influence the reaction-temperature fit?

# Starting point and strategy

The calorimetry preparation reads the canonical MEA observation table and
records the preceding endpoint for each finite-loading interval with the same
source, temperature, concentration and run. The retained partition contains
66 Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C calibration intervals, 20 Kim–Svendsen 120 °C
holdout intervals and 27 Kim et al. 2014 model-selection comparison rows.

Only six 40/80 °C intervals entered the reaction-temperature objective. The
120 °C block remained outside that fit, and Kim 2014 was comparison evidence.
Each interval is scored as the heat released per mole of CO₂ absorbed,
−[H_L(α₂) − H_L(α₁) − (α₂ − α₁) h_CO₂^ig(T)]/(α₂ − α₁), for 1 mol MEA, with
zero calorimeter vapor inventory and an ideal-gas CO₂ feed. The neutral
records cancel between the endpoints, so the result depends only on the EOS,
the reactions and their reference chain.

# Numerical result

::: {.parameter-table .numeric-table}
| Cohort | Intervals scored | RMSE (kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂) | Bias (kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C calibration | 63 / 66 | 11.77 | +0.4 |
| Kim–Svendsen 120 °C holdout | 20 / 20 | 29.28 | −15.8 |
| Kim 2014 comparison | 26 / 27 | 10.80 | +1.4 |
:::

Four 40 °C intervals start at loading 0.003 or 0.037, where the pinned Engine's
bubble solve ends infeasible from every start, including a 0.041 anchor. The
current Engine (wheel `ad12b19f`, after ePC-SAFT #154/#157) solves both states
from the packet start in three iterations; they are reported as failed here, not dropped.

On the same intervals the rebuilt values are 1.8–3.3 kJ mol⁻¹ above the
superseded-Engine anchored-reference values (RMSE 12.09, 31.15 and 10.87
before). The rebuilt enthalpy chain is closed: at 40, 80 and 120 °C and
loadings 0.1–0.5 its CO₂ feed action matches centered re-solves of the
enthalpy to ≤ 3.1 × 10⁻⁹ and equals RT²·∂ln a_CO₂/∂T + RT to ≤ 2.6 × 10⁻¹³
([thermal checks](../results/calorimetry/thermal-reference-validation.csv)).
The source of the superseded offset was not re-derived.

# Conclusion and limits

The 40/80 °C calibration intervals are unbiased on average (+0.4 kJ mol⁻¹)
with an 11.8 kJ mol⁻¹ scatter, while the 120 °C holdout is under-predicted by
15.8 kJ mol⁻¹ on average. Loaded-solution heat capacity is compared with Hilliard 2008 and Weiland 1997
in `verify_solution_heat_capacity`; pure liquid water cp from the ideal-gas
record and the EOS residual is 12–15 % below IAPWS-95, and pure MEA liquid cp
has no verified retained reference. The heat study identifies a remaining thermal discrepancy; it does
not justify refitting every EOS or reaction parameter.
